title: A transient toast maps its priority to the polite or assertive slot, announces once, and dismisses on activation or timeout
asA: screen-reader user reading a shipped rcf-lite application
iWant: an informational toast to reach me on the polite queue and an error toast to reach me on the assertive queue, each announced exactly once and dismissable on my activation or after a WCAG-compliant timeout
soThat: I can tell an interruption from a confirmation and I have time to read the message before it disappears

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a toast triggered by a background event with priority `info`, the toast renders inside `[data-live-region="polite"]` and carries `role="status"`; given priority `error`, the toast renders inside `[data-live-region="assertive"]` and carries `role="alert"`; every toast body text appears in exactly one wrapper (the one whose role reflects the priority) and never in both; every toast records `data-shown-at` and `data-dismissed-at` timestamps on its DOM element; the elapsed time between `data-shown-at` and `data-dismissed-at` on a toast that timed out (not clicked away) is at or above the ADR-2102 floor of six seconds. The pack enumerates toasts by `[data-toast-id]` inside the two wrappers (per-element attribute), not by `role` alone.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a toast triggered by a background event
acceptanceCriteria.when: the accessibility tree and the toast timestamps are read
acceptanceCriteria.then: the priority-to-role mapping holds, the announcement is one-shot, and the timeout is at or above the six second floor

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given the toast factory (TAC-2101 `renderToast({ priority, body })`), the factory picks the polite wrapper for `info` priority and the assertive wrapper for `error` priority; a factory that writes into both wrappers on one call, or picks the wrong wrapper for a priority, fails at project-side review.
acceptanceCriteria.when: the factory is invoked at a given priority
acceptanceCriteria.then: the correct wrapper receives the toast

acceptanceCriteria.description: Apply refuses a toast-timeout-floor answer below 6 seconds with TOAST_TIMEOUT_TOO_SHORT naming the elicited value; a value at or above 6 seconds applies and the polite toast honours it. Vendor citation on WCAG 2.2.1 (https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#timing-adjustable, verified 2026-09-10).
acceptanceCriteria.given: a project elicits a toast-timeout-floor below 6 seconds
acceptanceCriteria.then: apply exits with a non-zero code and TOAST_TIMEOUT_TOO_SHORT names the elicited value; at or above 6 seconds apply succeeds

acceptanceCriteria.description: A transient toast auto-dismisses at the elicited timeout only if the principal has not focused it; a focused toast pauses the timer and resumes only after focus leaves (WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable, https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#timing-adjustable, verified 2026-09-10).
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered toast and the principal focuses it via the keyboard
acceptanceCriteria.then: the toast remains visible until focus leaves; on focus loss the timer resumes
